A user reported having many problems with LangChain and said they are very happy since switching to Mastra.

A self-described happy Mastra user said it balances higher-level abstractions with lower-level control when needed. After looking at a handful of other frameworks, they found Mastra's clarity and ease of use stood out.
One user said they learned how agents work by using Mastra and reading its documentation, and that the founders are very hands-on and helpful.
A commenter said the abstractions address many pain points of building agents and that the team is eager to help.

A commenter pointed out that Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which forbids providing the software as a hosted or managed service. They argued this is not actually open source, despite the 'open-source' claim.
A critic said the workflow chaining example from the landing page (.step().then().after().then().commit()) looks like a very awkward way to represent a simple graph.
A skeptic said tool-orchestration frameworks like this cover only about 5% of the work, the trivial part. Developers still have to fill the other 95%, which is outside the framework's scope.
One commenter objected to Mastra being built on the Vercel AI SDK, saying 'It started off wrong.'
A user noted that only Stdio MCP servers were supported, not SSE MCP servers. As a workaround, they said they could run a proxy.
A user said they have been using Mastra for side projects for months and called it phenomenal.

A user who has built with Mastra for a few weeks said they are loving it. They felt building on the Vercel AI SDK was a good decision, describing the AI SDK as a low-level library and Mastra as a framework on top of it.

After three months with Mastra, a user called it awesome and best in class for TypeScript. However, workflows with branching logic and non-LLM, rules-based agents felt clunky. After a couple of weeks of frustration, they switched to their own custom branching workflows.

One team found Mastra batteries-included and opinionated, so productivity drops when you don't fit an existing pattern. They repeatedly had to create their own Hono routes and are now rebuilding with LangGraph/LangChain. They still credited Mastra's good ideas and its TypeScript-first approach.
A user ran through the quickstart and built a chat agent. They liked the UI and the systems but weren't sure what to build next.
A user praised the out-of-the-box developer experience but said the pricing page doesn't seem to show any prices.
A user whose entire stack is TypeScript welcomed a production-grade agent framework with no vendor lock-in.
A commenter cautioned that although Mastra avoids model lock-in, users are likely locked into a platform instead. In their view, the convenience just shifts where the lock-in occurs in the stack.
A commenter pointed to the Brex CTO describing Mastra as part of Brex's AI engineering stack, offered as an independent endorsement.
StepSecurity's threat intelligence team reported that multiple Mastra npm packages had been compromised.
